_note: Errands: safe idle jobs you put resting pets on (the errands tab, opened by the little basket). Nobody is ever lost on an errand. Every job works the same way: a meter fills once every 'seconds' with one pet, faster with more (crew size ^ 'crew_power', so each extra pet helps a little less and spreading pets out beats stacking them), and pays 'pay' each time it's full. PAY: 'capsules' is worth that many of the capsule machine's plain capsules (Machine.coin_value), so every machine upgrade raises errands too and idle coins keep up with the machine all game (tune it well under pulling); 'coins' a fixed [min, max]; 'part' a common part each fill ('uncommon' gives a chance of an uncommon part once the crew is big enough). 'tips' multiplies a job's pay by its crew's average rarity (the lemonade stand: cute pets get bigger tips). A pet's 'stat' nudges how fast it works (rarer pets have higher stats, see Jobs.pet_speed), and 'traits' multiply it. Errands never bring rare parts or new places: those only come from adventures. Offline they run at full speed for 'offline_full_hours', then at 'offline_after' speed. 'color' is a UiTheme role, 'doodle' a UiTheme doodle. 'needs' is an unlock id (data/unlocks.json 'opens') a job waits for: until then it isn't there (the scrapyard waits for parts, a late feature; the lemonade stand opens at coin hunt lv 10). TOOLS are what coins buy on the upgrades page (the pegboard): a job's own 'tools', and the top-level 'tools' for every job. Each level costs 'coins' x 'grow' to the power of the levels you have; 'max' 0 means no end; 'at' is the job level it waits for; 'machine' a machine tree node it waits for. 'each' is what every level does: worth (+capsules a fill), speed (fills this much sooner, added up), big (chance per fill of a big one: x 'big_x'), rare_x (tips of rare-or-better pets count this many times), all_speed (every job faster), away_hours (more hours at full speed while you're away), shiny (errand finds are shiny as often as the machine's balls, and pay like them), crew_power (each extra pet on a job helps more). A job's LEVEL is all its tools' levels added up; its 'goals' are reached at a level: 'x' multiplies its pay from then on, 'text' says what happens (an unlock with earn 'job_level' opens then). Numbers are placeholders until tools/balance.gd tunes them.
